rawFindings.title: AUTH callback is skipped on authentication failure
rawFindings.explanation: When do_auth receives an AUTH error, this line now always emits an error instead of invoking the callback saved by client.auth(pass, callback). The auth method still stores auth_callback and the success path still invokes it, so callers using the documented command-callback pattern no longer receive failures through their callback.
rawFindings.suggestion: Before emitting, check self.auth_callback, call it with the original error, clear it, and return; only emit when no callback is registered.
rawFindings.failureAfterChange: Against a password-protected Redis server, `client = redis.createClient(); client.auth('wrong', function (err) { called = true; }); client.on('error', function() {});` results in the error event firing while `called` remains false.
